root_idea.summary: A downward extension or elongated incision, producing the related ideas of cheek, furrow, trench, groove, and wasting or wrinkling flesh.
root_idea.development: The root develops from the notion of something extending or being drawn downward: the cheek is a lateral facial extension, while a furrow or trench is an elongated incision in the ground. Further derivatives describe marks, grooves, leanness, and division into distinct bodies.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested noun meaning a trench or deep excavated furrow.
Distinct Quran-attested noun meaning the cheek.

senses.definition: An elongated furrow, trench, or deep excavated hollow in the ground; in the Quranic usage, the fire-filled trench into which believers were cast.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence refers specifically to the trench associated with the people of the trench; the broader lexical sense includes a deep fissure, channel, hole, cavity, or pit in the ground.

senses.definition: The cheek: the lateral part of the face on either side of the nose and mouth.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence it is the cheek whose turning away from people is prohibited. The supplied QAC analysis identifies the form as a noun, despite its surface spelling resembling a verbal form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To furrow, trench, or cleave the ground; of a torrent, to furrow the ground by its course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive ground-cutting use, with a corresponding use for a torrent cutting the ground by flowing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mark, score, or impress a thing, leaving a line, furrow, or other impression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning includes marks made upon the ground or upon a cheek, without restricting the use to any particular marking agent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cleave or cut a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cleaving use is also attested of an animal cutting with a tusk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For flesh to contract, wrinkle, waste, become flaccid, or show furrow-like streaks; to render someone lean, wasted, or impaired in condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The flesh use describes wasting and wrinkling; extended uses describe travel or adverse conditions producing leanness or deterioration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To oppose or resist another, including by becoming angry against him and opposing his work or conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or adversarial opposition is expressed toward another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the ground to become furrowed or cleft by a torrent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive resultative use describing ground cut by flowing water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For people to become divided into distinct bodies or parties.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative social use describing separation into recognizable groups.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To oppose one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal opposition between two or more parties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plank forming one of the side boards of a howdah or similar vehicle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized object sense, with the plural forms خِدَاد and خِدَّان also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A side or lateral portion of rugged elevated ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The geographical sense extends the side-or-face notion to land and other things by figurative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An assembly, company, rank, class, race, or generation of people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can denote a congregated body or successive ranks or generations, as in rank after rank.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal geographical use distinct from the facial sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mark made with a hot iron upon the cheek of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A branding-mark term associated specifically with the cheek.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rivulet or streamlet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A watercourse sense related to a channel or furrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The main, middle, or open tracks of a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The track sense is explained as arising from the furrows made by the feet of people or animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Furrows, grooves, or marks, including grooves made by well-ropes and furrows left by whips.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are elongated marks or channels produced by drawing, repeated movement, or striking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A blow, stroke, or beating that furrows the skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for a striking action whose result is a furrowed mark.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A canine tooth or tush; each of the two tushes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular denotes one tooth, while the pair is termed مِخَدَّان.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pillow or cushion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is so named because it is placed beneath the cheek.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An iron implement used to furrow, trench, or cleave the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tool sense derived from the action of making a furrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel bearing the cheek-mark called خِدَاد.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial description of an animal marked on the cheek.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lean or emaciated, with little flesh; also describing a body that is wasted and furrowed or wrinkled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of wasting and the resulting furrowed appearance of the body.

cautions: The Classical evidence notes a possible transcription issue in the plural form cited for the road-track usage; the lexical track meaning is retained without resolving that textual variant.
